content:
cheng: seeing intermittent PCIe AER/Xid spikes + NVLink link flaps on pool9 (rack7). Batch jobs show elevated tail latency and a bunch of retries. Noticed around 02:14 UTC. Posting quick logs below.

ops-bot: ALERT: elevated_xid_errors detected on cluster-pool9 (threshold breached)

mike: which nodes in pool9? can you paste the dmesg snippet you saw?

cheng: here's the small dmesg slice (just the noisy bits):
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 62, PID: 4151, Tx: 0x0e
[ 1234.568001] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: ID 0000
[ 1234.570123] nvlink: nvlink: link 2 gone (down) on GPU 00000000:3B:00.0
[ 1234.571456] nvlink: nvlink: link 2 up at reduced width
[ 1234.572789] NVRM: GPU 00000000:3B:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
```

karla: temps/fans showing anything odd? PSU?

cheng: temps steady ~54-58C, fans normal. No PSU logs. No recent power-cycling on those nodes.

sanjay: looks like link negotiation drops then comes back w/ reduced width. Could be a flaky riser/contact, or transient AER noise. Steps: (1) drain suspect GPU(s) from scheduling, (2) reseat GPU (if still flapping), (3) run `nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR` and `dmesg -T | grep -i nvlink` for full trace, (4) RMA if persists.

mike: agree. cheng, can you identify the specific hostnames? we should isolate one node first.

cheng: nodes affected: gpu-7-02, gpu-7-03, gpu-7-06 (same top-of-rack). Running quick error query now:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR
GPU 0000:3B:00.0
    XID Errors: 5 since boot
    Corrected Error Count: 12
    Uncorrected Error Count: 0

$ lspci -vvv -s 00:1c.0 | grep AER
    AER:   Device status: Corrected+Non-Fatal+First Error
```

karla: ok please start draining gpu-7-02 first. route its jobs to pool11. @oncall-bot can you shift batch routing for pool9->pool11 for affected slots?

oncall-bot: reroute-batcher: initiated. Redirecting 3 capacity units from pool9 to pool11. ETA ~90s.

sanjay: I'll create an INF ticket to track diag + spare swap if reseat fails. If errors continue after reseat -> schedule RMA for the card and escalate to hardware vendor. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2147

mike: quick triage checklist for field team: 1) reseat card, 2) reseat riser, 3) swap to known-good slot, 4) test with `nvlink --status` (or driver logs) while running short memtest workload. If flaps stop on reseat -> monitor for 24h.

cheng: starting drain on gpu-7-02 now, will run reseat window if flaps persist. collecting full diag tarball and will attach to INF-2147. Thanks. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: NOTE: job latency for pool9 decreased by 18% after reroute (metrics pipeline).
